speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the appearance of your skin lesions in detail, including their size, color, and whether they are itchy or bleeding. Also, how long have you noticed these changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; the combination of a non-healing penile lesion and a digit lesion in a smoker raises concern for Squamous Cell Carcinoma. REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC) and HIV serology. Are you currently taking any medications or immunosuppressants?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: Normal; HIV Serology: Negative

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats, or malaise. No other similar lesions elsewhere on the body. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That report regarding pneumonia seems inconsistent with your history of non-healing skin lesions; pneumonia would present with respiratory symptoms, not penile or digital ulcers. Given your heavy smoking history and the specific nature of these lesions, we must rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the penile lesion and REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up dermoscopy of the finger lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Invasive Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and digital). The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitosis confirm malignancy. Given the patient's age, heavy smoking history, and African origin, I need to check for HIV status to assess for immunosuppression which may influence staging and treatment.
